confirmed: Version: Oregon State Ecampus Research Unit, Research Fellows white paper dated April 2025, 23 pages; title and authors (J.T. Bushnell, Wayne Harrison) match (p. 1; p. 23, Suggested Citation, '[White Paper]').

No study randomizes people: every student did all three conditions in one fixed sequence, Condition 1 in Week 7, Condition 2 in Week 8, Condition 3 after three video lessons and a 10-question quiz with the prompt 'Like you did in the last exercise' (pp. 6-7); the survey labels both ChatGPT exercises 'Week 8' (Appendix 2, p. 21).

The only randomization is the order in which samples went to the judges (p. 5, Data Collection; p. 22, Appendix 3). design_class quasi_people, randomized 'no', criterion 1 not_met, and context_class observational are correct; has_randomized_people_study is false.

Counts: sections enrolled 22 and 24 (46 possible); 40 consented (about 87%); 9 removed; 31 analyzed with 93 writing samples; n = 31 in each condition (pp. 4-5, Participant Recruitment; p. 5, Table 1; p. 8, Exploratory Data Analysis). n_randomized null is right; 31 is below 50, so criterion 2 is not_met.

Outcome: two expert judges (college creative-writing instructors who did not teach the courses), blind to writer and condition, rated each sample 1-7 and then agreed on a consensus score (Consensual Assessment Technique); Krippendorff's alpha 0.80 (pp. 7-8, Evaluation Criteria). overall_creativity, expert_raters, with_ai, and criterion 3 met are correct.

AI tool GPT-4o (p. 4, Method); the Condition 2 and 3 prompts and the 10 suggested prompts match ai_tool.how_used and task.description (pp. 6-7). IRB approval HE-2024-811 is stated and no preregistration is mentioned (p. 4).
Table 3 (p. 8): Baseline (1) 3.61, SD 1.20, SE 0.22; ChatGPT (2) 3.52, 0.77, 0.14; ChatGPT + Instructor (3) 4.32, 1.33, 0.24; ns = 31. Matches the reported string.
Table 4 (p. 9): Condition SS 12.02, df 2, MS 6.01, F 5.01, p 0.01, eta2 0.14, residual df 60; text gives F (2, 60) = 5.01, p = .01. Matches.

Table 5 (p. 9, Bonferroni-adjusted p): 1 vs 2: 0.01, SE 0.26, t 0.37, p 1.00, D 0.09; 1 vs 3: -0.71, 0.28, -2.51, .05, 0.63; 2 vs 3: -0.81, 0.29, -2.81, .03, 0.72. Matches; the form's note that 0.01 does not equal 3.61 - 3.52 is accurate.
Table 6 (p. 10) totals 3.88, 3.55, 4.34 differ from Table 3, as the form says.
One-line finding: 3.61, 3.52, 4.32, p = 1.00, p = .05, p = .03 all match Tables 3 and 5 (pp. 8-9).
No company involvement: the authors say they were not paid or otherwise influenced by OpenAI (p. 17, Conflicts of Interest).

Checker computation from Appendix 3 (p. 22), not printed in the paper: means 3.61, 3.52, 4.32 and SDs 1.20, 0.77, 1.33 reproduce Table 3, and score counts 0/12/27/29/17/7/1 reproduce Table 2. Paired differences are 1-2 = 0.10 (SE 0.26, t 0.37), 1-3 = -0.71 (SE 0.28, t -2.51), 2-3 = -0.81 (SE 0.29, t -2.81), so the printed 0.01 in Table 5 looks like a misprint for about 0.10.

Checker computation from Appendix 3: the low group's Condition 1 mean is 2.53, not the 2.43 printed in Table 6 (Figure 2, p. 11, plots it near 2.5). With 2.53, the unweighted mean of the three starting-level means gives Table 6's totals (3.88, 3.55, 4.34), which explains why they differ from Table 3.
summary: The form correctly codes c227 as a fixed-order, non-randomized within-subjects study of 31 students (quasi_people, observational context, criteria 1 and 2 not met), and every number in its reported string and one-line finding matches Tables 3-5 on pp. 8-9. Five corrections concern completeness: statistics_available is empty although Tables 3 and 5 print means, SDs, SEs, t, p, and Cohen's D; the supplement field misses Appendices 1-3 in the PDF (Appendix 3, p. 22, lists all 31 participants' scores); the 3-vs-1 and 3-vs-2 contrasts lack entries; exclusions is blank; and the participants quote runs 42 words.
